question.text: Swasth Bharat Trust (healthcare NPO) reports the following in its most recent audited FY: Total receipts Rs. 8 lakh; Total payments Rs. 42 lakh; Corpus fund Rs. 2.5 crore. As SIA, which of the two MANDATORY fund-flow thresholds does Swasth Bharat FAIL under Table 3.1?

answer.text: Fails the Spending threshold (Rs. 50 lakh minimum) only
Fails the Funding threshold (Rs. 10 lakh minimum) only
Fails BOTH the Spending AND the Funding thresholds
Passes both thresholds because corpus exceeds Rs. 1 crore

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Table 3.1 requires Annual Spending >= Rs. 50 lakh AND Funding received >= Rs. 10 lakh in the past FY. Swasth Bharat's payments of Rs. 42 lakh fail the Rs. 50 lakh Spending threshold; receipts of Rs. 8 lakh fail the Rs. 10 lakh Funding threshold. BOTH limbs fail. Corpus size is irrelevant to this test (corpus is measured at a point in time; spending/funding are flows). **The Trap:** Option A misses the funding limb. Option B misses the spending limb. Option D is a classic corpus-vs-flow conflation — a common mistake. The SIA must test the FLOWS, not the stock. **Cross-Exam Context:** X-A/X-B (IA) test trust corpus vs income application under Section 11(1)(a). XV (RA) uses corpus size for valuation. SSE specifically tests FLOW thresholds. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** In your pre-engagement acceptance checklist, explicitly write the 50/10 rule and compute both flows before accepting. Many NPOs think a high corpus buys time — it doesn't. Advise them to defer SSE onboarding until a full FY of qualifying operations crosses both thresholds.
